stories.headline: Kuaishou's Kling AI raises ~$2.8B in largest-ever AI video round at $15B pre-money

key_facts.fact: Kuaishou secured 19 billion yuan ($2.8 billion) for its AI video-generation unit Kling AI, valuing the business at $15 billion before the investment.
key_facts.excerpt: Kuaishou Technology has secured 19 billion yuan ($2.8 billion) for its artificial intelligence (AI) video-generation unit, Kling AI, in a funding round that values the business at $15 billion before the investment.

key_facts.fact: The financing remains open to more investors and aims to raise a total of $3 billion for a 16.7% stake; Kuaishou called it the largest round ever completed by an AI video model developer globally.
key_facts.excerpt: The financing, which remains open to additional investors, aims to raise a total of $3 billion in exchange for a 16.7% stake in the business... the largest ever completed by a developer of AI video models globally.

key_facts.fact: Investors include Alibaba Group, Tencent ($200 million), Baidu, CPE, CITIC Securities and others; the round dilutes Kuaishou's stake in Kling to about 68%.

key_facts.fact: Kling's annual recurring revenue grew to about $500 million in March from $300 million in January after the Kling 3.0 launch; Q1 revenue topped 650 million yuan ($96.2 million), up more than 300% year over year.
key_facts.excerpt: The division's annual recurring revenue... grew to about $500 million in March from $300 million in January, driven by the launch of Kling 3.0. It generated revenue of over 650 million yuan ($96.2 million) in the first quarter, up more than 300% from a year ago.

key_facts.fact: The round confers a post-money valuation of about $18 billion; Kling is being spun off as an independent business with an IPO targeted for 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: Tencent is among the investors in the round, which values the company at roughly 18 billion dollars on a post-money basis... The Information has reported an IPO is being targeted for 2027.

key_facts.fact: Wang said Watermelon is currently in training and uses an order of magnitude more compute than Avocado, Meta's internal codename for the Muse Spark model.

stories.headline: Alibaba bans employees from using Claude Code from July 10 over alleged backdoor

key_facts.fact: Alibaba will bar employees from using Anthropic's Claude Code in workplace environments from July 10, citing alleged security risks involving embedded backdoors.
key_facts.excerpt: Alibaba will ban employees from using Claude Code in workspace environments from July 10 due to alleged security risks involving embedded backdoors, a source familiar with the matter said.

key_facts.fact: The move was first reported by Chinese financial outlet Yicai and corroborated by Reuters through its own source; Alibaba did not confirm it publicly.
key_facts.excerpt: The ban was first reported by the Chinese financial outlet Yicai before Reuters corroborated it through its own source.

key_facts.fact: Alibaba internally ordered employees to uninstall all Anthropic products, including the Claude Sonnet, Opus and Fable model series and the Claude Code agent tool, effective July 10.
key_facts.excerpt: Alibaba has internally ordered all employees to uninstall Anthropic products, including the Claude Sonnet, Opus, and Fable model series as well as the Claude Code agent tool, with the ban taking effect on July 10.

key_facts.fact: The ban follows Anthropic's June 10 letter to US senators alleging Alibaba- and Qwen-linked operators ran nearly 25,000 fraudulent accounts to generate more than 28.8 million exchanges with Claude between April 22 and June 5 in a model-distillation campaign.
key_facts.excerpt: In a letter dated June 10 to US senators, Anthropic accused operators connected to Alibaba's Qwen AI lab of running nearly 25,000 fraudulent accounts to extract Claude's software engineering and reasoning capabilities, generating more than 28.8 million exchanges between April 22 and June 5.

key_facts.fact: Developers found Claude Code had embedded a detection mechanism from version 2.1.91 (April 2026); a Claude Code team member said it was meant to curb account reselling and distillation and would be removed in the next release.
key_facts.excerpt: A member of its Claude Code team, Thariq, is reported to have responded on social media that the mechanism was meant to curb account reselling and model distillation, and that it would be stripped out in the next release.

stories.headline: Chip group SEMI urges US not to intervene in memory market as AI drives shortage

key_facts.fact: SEMI sent a letter dated July 1 to senior Trump administration officials arguing the government should not intervene directly in the memory chip market and should instead focus on expanding production.
key_facts.excerpt: The global industry association SEMI stated in a letter sent on July 1 (local time) to senior officials of the Donald Trump administration, 'Policies to enhance the resilience of domestic supply chains can be helpful, but interventions that distort prices or production capacity risk prolonging the shortage.'

key_facts.fact: SEMI warned that as high-bandwidth memory (HBM) production for AI data centers expands, general DRAM capacity is shrinking, worsening shortages across laptops, smartphones, automobiles, home appliances and defense.
key_facts.excerpt: SEMI diagnosed that as production of high-bandwidth memory (HBM) for AI data centers expands, general DRAM production capacity is decreasing, which is exacerbating memory supply shortages across a range of industries.

key_facts.fact: SEMI projected memory production capacity will grow about 19% per year on average but expects AI infrastructure demand to outpace that, keeping shortages and price pressure in place.
key_facts.excerpt: SEMI projected that memory production capacity will increase by about 19% per year on average, but the pace of AI infrastructure demand growth is expected to outstrip this.

key_facts.fact: The letter came as Apple asked the US government to let it procure memory from China's CXMT and YMTC to ease shortages; SEMI's members include Micron, Samsung, SK hynix, Intel and TSMC across 3,000-plus companies.
key_facts.excerpt: The letter came as Apple asked the U.S. government to cooperate so it can procure memory from China's CXMT and YMTC to ease shortages... With Micron in the United States, Samsung Electronics, and SK hynix all participating as members.

key_facts.fact: As alternatives to intervention, SEMI proposed working with Congress to expand long-term supply contracts, extend tax incentives for US production, and introduce consumer tax credits to offset rising phone and laptop prices.
key_facts.excerpt: SEMI believes that... allowing memory semiconductor companies to continue long-term contracts with customers and providing tax credits would alleviate price pressure.

key_facts.fact: It was the deadliest attack on the capital this year, killing at least 30 by some counts and damaging around 130 buildings
key_facts.excerpt: Russia launched hundreds of drones and dozens of missiles at Ukraine's capital Kyiv in the early hours of Thursday, July 2, killing at least 30 people, wounding scores more and damaging around 130 buildings in the deadliest attack on the capital this year.

key_facts.fact: The Ukrainian Air Force said Russia fired 570 drones and missiles overnight, including 496 Shahed/Gerbera/Italmas strike drones, 24 Iskander-M/S-400 ballistic missiles and 34 Kh-101 cruise missiles; Ukraine downed 476 drones
key_facts.excerpt: Russian forces launched 570 drones and missiles, including 496 Shahed-, Gerbera-, and Italmas-type strike drones ... 24 Iskander-M/S-400 ballistic missiles; 34 Kh-101 cruise missiles ... Ukrainian forces downed 476 drones.

key_facts.fact: Zelensky vowed Ukraine would 'definitely' retaliate, visited a damaged apartment block, and pressed the US for licences to manufacture Patriot air-defence missiles
key_facts.excerpt: President Volodymyr Zelensky vowed Thursday to retaliate for Russia's deadly strikes ... 'We also very much count on a decision by the United States regarding licences for Patriots.'

key_facts.fact: EU foreign-policy chief Kaja Kallas said she would propose new sanctions on entities supporting Russia's military-industrial complex in response to the strike
key_facts.excerpt: 'Today, I will propose to sanction more entities supporting Russia's military-industrial complex in response to the strikes,' she said in a post on X.

key_facts.fact: Moscow said the bombardment was retaliation for Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil facilities; overnight Ukraine struck the Lukoil-Nizhegorodnefteorgsintez refinery in Russia's Nizhny Novgorod region
key_facts.excerpt: Ukraine struck one of Russia's largest oil refineries and targets in Russian-occupied territories ... hit the Lukoil-Nizhnesintez oil refinery in the city of Kstovo in Russia's Nizhny Oblast.

stories.headline: US June payrolls rise just 57,000 as hiring cools, cutting odds of a Fed rate hike

key_facts.fact: US nonfarm payrolls rose by 57,000 in June, about half of what markets expected
key_facts.excerpt: Nonfarm payroll growth slowed in June to 57,000 jobs—half as many as expected.

key_facts.fact: The unemployment rate fell to 4.2% from 4.3% in May, its lowest since June 2025, driven mainly by people leaving the labor force rather than by job creation
key_facts.excerpt: The U.S. unemployment rate fell from 4.3% in May to 4.2% in June ... The modest decline in unemployment was driven primarily by fewer people entering the labor force.

key_facts.fact: Prior-month gains were revised sharply lower: April cut by 31,000 (to 148,000) and May by 43,000 (to 129,000); participation and the employment-population ratio fell to levels last seen in 2021
key_facts.excerpt: April's estimate was revised down by 31,000 jobs (from 179,000 to 148,000), and May's estimate was revised down by 43,000 jobs (from 172,000 to 129,000) ... the labor force participation rate and employment-population ratio both fell to levels last seen in 2021.

key_facts.fact: The soft data cut the market-implied probability of a July Fed rate hike to about 20%, down from 33% before the report, and Treasury yields declined across the curve
key_facts.excerpt: Markets have recalibrated expectations, reducing the probability of a July rate hike to approximately 20% ... U.S. Treasury yields declined across the curve.

key_facts.fact: Fed funds futures late Thursday implied roughly even odds of a hike by the September meeting, and the dollar slipped as traders pared expectations for near-term tightening
key_facts.excerpt: Fed fund futures late on Thursday suggested roughly even odds that the central bank would raise rates by its September meeting ... the dollar slipped as traders pared expectations for a rate hike as early as September.

stories.headline: Roche's divarasib beats approved KRAS G12C drugs in Phase III lung-cancer trial

key_facts.fact: On July 2 Roche reported positive Phase III (Krascendo 1) results for divarasib, an investigational next-generation KRAS G12C inhibitor, in previously treated advanced KRAS G12C non-small cell lung cancer
key_facts.excerpt: Roche announced today positive results from the phase III Krascendo 1 study evaluating divarasib, an investigational next-generation KRAS G12C inhibitor ... in patients with previously treated KRAS G12C non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC).

key_facts.fact: In a head-to-head trial against approved first-generation inhibitors sotorasib or adagrasib, divarasib met its primary endpoint (progression-free survival) and key secondary endpoint (overall survival) with clinically meaningful, statistically significant improvements
key_facts.excerpt: The study met its primary and key secondary endpoint, with divarasib achieving clinically meaningful and statistically significant improvements in both progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS).

key_facts.fact: Statistical significance for overall survival was reached at the interim analysis in this poor-prognosis population, with no new safety signals observed
key_facts.excerpt: Statistical significance for overall survival was achieved at the interim analysis in this poor-prognosis patient population ... no new safety signals were observed.

key_facts.fact: The FDA granted divarasib Breakthrough Therapy Designation in 2022 and Orphan Drug Designation for KRAS G12C NSCLC in 2026; Roche said the data will be submitted to health authorities
key_facts.excerpt: The US Food and Drug Administration granted Breakthrough Therapy Designation to divarasib in 2022, and in 2026, Orphan Drug Designation for KRAS G12C non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC).

sources.title: Roche's divarasib shows superiority in head-to-head phase III trial against approved KRAS G12C inhibitors in NSCLC

stories.headline: NASA's rescue mission to save the Swift space telescope grounded by rocket glitch

key_facts.fact: On July 2 a rush mission to rescue NASA's Swift space telescope remained grounded after a last-minute problem prevented release of the Pegasus rocket
key_facts.excerpt: A rush rescue mission to save a NASA space telescope remains grounded, this time because of a last-minute launch problem.

key_facts.fact: Northrop Grumman's rocket-launching plane took off from the Marshall Islands in the Pacific, but an issue stopped the team from dropping the Pegasus rocket strapped to the plane's belly
key_facts.excerpt: Northrop Grumman's rocket-launching plane took off from the Marshall Islands in the Pacific on Thursday ... But an issue prevented the team from releasing the Pegasus rocket strapped to the plane's belly.

key_facts.fact: The Pegasus carries a three-armed robotic spacecraft built by Katalyst Space Technologies to grapple the Swift Observatory and boost it to a higher orbit
key_facts.excerpt: The rocket holds a three-armed robotic spacecraft built by Katalyst Space Technologies to capture the Swift Observatory, which will come crashing down by October if no help arrives.

key_facts.fact: Without intervention Swift will re-enter and crash by October; NASA hired Katalyst last September for the roughly $30 million salvage of the telescope, which launched in 2004 and has detected thousands of gamma-ray bursts
key_facts.excerpt: Anxious to continue Swift's scanning of the universe, the space agency hired Katalyst Space last September for the $30 million salvage operation ... It has detected thousands of gamma ray bursts and exploding stars since its launch in 2004.

key_facts.fact: No new launch date was set after the scrub, though the next attempt could come as early as July 3
key_facts.excerpt: Poised on a tarmac on the Kwajalein Atoll ... and set to fly as early as tomorrow, July 3, is an L-1011 Stargazer jet, carrying a three-stage Pegasus rocket under its belly.

sources.title: Last-minute launch problem delays satellite rescue mission for NASA
Why NASA Is Launching a Mission to Save a Quarter-Billion Dollar Space Telescope

stories.headline: EU's top court upholds Google's record €4.1B Android antitrust fine, ending appeals

key_facts.fact: On July 2 the Court of Justice of the EU dismissed Google and Alphabet's appeal, upholding a €4.1 billion (about $4.7 billion) fine for using Android to block rivals
key_facts.excerpt: Europe's top court has ruled Google must pay a €4.1bn (£3.5bn) fine handed down for using its Android mobile operating system to block rivals.

key_facts.fact: The European Commission originally imposed a €4.34 billion fine in 2018; the General Court trimmed it to €4.1 billion in 2022, and it remains the EU's largest-ever antitrust penalty
key_facts.excerpt: The findings were upheld in 2022 by the General Court ... But the Luxembourg-based body slightly reduced the levy to €4.1 billion – still the EU's biggest ever.

key_facts.fact: Regulators found Google required Android device makers to pre-install Google Search and Chrome as a condition of Play Store access, paid manufacturers for exclusive pre-installation, and blocked 'forked' versions of Android
key_facts.excerpt: requiring Android handset and tablet manufacturers to pre-install the Google Search app and its own web browser Chrome as a condition of allowing them to offer access to its Play app store ... preventing manufacturers from selling any smart devices powered by alternative 'forked' versions of Android.

key_facts.fact: A Google spokesperson said the judgment 'fails to recognise' the firm's investment to keep Android open, interoperable and free
key_facts.excerpt: A Google spokesperson said the judgement 'fails to recognise' the firm's 'significant investment to ensure Android remains open, interoperable and free'.

key_facts.fact: The court ordered Google to pay the Commission's legal costs; the case is C-738/22 P Google and Alphabet v Commission
key_facts.excerpt: 'The appeal brought by Google and its parent company Alphabet against the judgment of the General Court is dismissed' ... The case is C-738/22 P Google and Alphabet v Commission.

stories.headline: United Therapeutics buys Thymmune for $140M to add regenerative thymic cell therapies

key_facts.fact: On July 2 United Therapeutics (Nasdaq: UTHR) announced it acquired Thymmune Therapeutics, a privately held, preclinical-stage biotech developing scalable regenerative thymic cell therapies
key_facts.excerpt: United Therapeutics Corporation (Nasdaq: UTHR) announced today it has acquired Thymmune Therapeutics, Inc. (Thymmune), a privately held, preclinical stage biotechnology company developing scalable, regenerative thymic cell therapies.

key_facts.fact: United Therapeutics paid $140 million in cash plus potential earn-out payments of up to $160 million tied to clinical and regulatory milestones by the end of 2031
key_facts.excerpt: United Therapeutics acquired Thymmune for $140 million in cash, subject to certain post-closing adjustments, plus potential earn-out payments to former Thymmune equityholders of up to $160 million based upon the achievement of certain clinical and regulatory milestones by the end of 2031.

key_facts.fact: Thymmune's therapies target post-transplant organ tolerance, immunodeficiencies and autoimmune diseases
key_facts.excerpt: developing scalable, regenerative thymic cell therapies for the potential treatment of post-transplant organ tolerance, immunodeficiencies, and autoimmune diseases.

stories.headline: Brent slides to pre-war low near $70 as Gulf supply recovers, OPEC+ weighs output hike

key_facts.fact: Brent crude fell to about $70.8 a barrel on July 2, its lowest since February 27 — the day before the US-Israel war on Iran began — leaving it down more than 38% from a post-war peak above $126 on April 30
key_facts.excerpt: Brent futures for August delivery stood at $70.82 per barrel ... lower than at any point since February 27, the day before the war began ... Brent prices are down more than 38 percent from their post-war peak of more than $126 a barrel on April 30.

key_facts.fact: Saudi Arabia restored crude loadings to almost 90% of pre-war levels, with four supertankers carrying about 8 million barrels exiting the Strait of Hormuz on Thursday — the most in a single day since the mid-June memorandum
key_facts.excerpt: Four supertankers carrying about 8 million barrels of crude from the kingdom's main export terminal at Ras Tanura entered the Gulf of Oman on Thursday ... the largest number of supertankers exiting the Strait of Hormuz in a single day since the memorandum was signed in mid-June.

key_facts.fact: A US official estimated oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz have recovered to more than 10 million barrels per day, still below the roughly 18-19 million bpd that transited before the war
key_facts.excerpt: oil supply through the Strait of Hormuz chokepoint has now reached more than 10 million barrels a day ... still well below the roughly 18 million to 19 million bpd that transited the waterway before the war.

key_facts.fact: OPEC+ is expected to approve another output increase of roughly 188,000 bpd for August at its weekend meeting — a fifth consecutive monthly hike
key_facts.excerpt: the producer group is expected to increase output quotas by approximately 188,000 barrels per day starting in August ... it would mark the fifth consecutive monthly production increase.

key_facts.fact: OPEC cut its 2026 global oil-demand-growth forecast for a second straight month, to 970,000 bpd from 1.17 million
key_facts.excerpt: OPEC recently lowered its 2026 global oil demand growth forecast for a second consecutive month, cutting its estimate from 1.17 million to 970,000 barrels per day.
